messages:
maya: Heads-up — started seeing a cluster-wide uptick in GPU pods Pending in us-west2. Cluster autoscaler is repeatedly adding nodes but they show up NotReady/NoSchedule.
lucas: Seen it too. I can repro on a new node: kubelet shows GPU device plugin crashloop, logs show socket bind errors.
maya: Logs? paste a snippet
lucas: ```
I0315 10:12:03.123456 1 plugin.go:98] starting device plugin
E0315 10:12:03.124000 1 plugin.go:112] failed to bind to unix socket /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/nvidia.sock: bind: address already in use
F0315 10:12:03.124100 1 main.go:45] plugin exiting: cannot create listener
``` 
priya: That's interesting — address already in use means another process holds it. Did the previous device-plugin not exit cleanly on the node image upgrade? We rolled a kernel patch last night.
maya: Autoscaler adds nodes, node joins, kubelet launches dp, dp immediately crashes -> node gets NoSchedule taint from gpu plugin failing readiness check. Autoscaler keeps adding nodes until we hit quota and pods stay Pending.
infra-bot: [alert] GPU node pool us-west2-gpu-pool scaling stalled: 6/8 new nodes NotReady (device-plugin crashloops)
ops-oncall: I temporarily reduced cluster-autoscaler aggressive scale-up (now 2 nodes) to avoid blowing quota. Will revert once fixed.
lucas: Quick workaround: stop kubelet, remove stale socket, restart kubelet. Did that on one node and the plugin came up fine.
maya: Steps you ran?
lucas: ```bash
ssh node-42
sudo systemctl stop kubelet
sudo rm -f /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/nvidia.sock
sudo systemctl start kubelet
kubectl get nodes -w # wait for Ready
``` 
priya: We need a robust fix. Suspect the device-plugin is racing with container runtime / kubelet socket GC on cgroupv2 nodes. The plugin tries to bind before the kubelet cleaned the previous socket.
maya: Any kubelet logs indicating slow cleanup? lucas, can you paste kubelet around that time
lucas: ```
E0315 10:11:59.987 kubelet.go:1234] failed to remove stale plugin socket: unlink /var/lib/kubelet/device-plugins/nvidia.sock: permission denied
``` 
priya: ah permission denied — systemd restart ordering might be wrong with our new init script. A race + permission error -> socket left behind.
ops-oncall: For immediate relief I cordoned the worst nodes and drained pending critical pods to the healthy pool. Not ideal but buys time.
maya: Proposed permanent fixes:
- update device-plugin image to 1.5.2 which retries bind with exponential backoff
- add a preStop hook to device-plugin that ensures socket cleanup
- tweak node image systemd unit to stop plugin before kubelet restart and fix permissions
- add a cluster-autoscaler safety cap to avoid quota burn
priya: Agree. Also add a readinessProbe that checks socket ownership to avoid NoSchedule taint flapping.
lucas: I'll open a PR with the plugin bump + preStop. Will include a small init-script change and systemd drop-in to fix ordering.
maya: Can we roll the fix as a canary to one AZ first? We should avoid mass-rollout when autoscaler is sensitive.
ops-oncall: I'll temporarily bump quota headroom and reduce CA aggressive:scaleDownDelay to buy time for canary.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: started canary rollout of node-image w/ device-plugin:tag=1.5.2 to us-west2-a (1/4 nodes)
lucas: Canary node came up Ready after the change. Plugin no longer crashloops and socket present with correct perms.
maya: Nice — after canary looks good let's schedule a controlled rollout and revert CA caps afterwards.
priya: Filing a follow-up runbook: how to handle device-plugin socket races and a playbook for quick remediation (cordon/drain, rm socket, restart kubelet). I'll post it to #help and link here.
maya: Great. Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread open until full rollout complete. :thumbsup:
